successCriteria.description: LeaveBalance interface is defined in src/modules/leave/leave-balance.model.ts with all required fields: id (string), employeeId (string), policyId (string), totalEntitlement (number), usedDays (number), remainingDays (number), pendingDays (number), fiscalYear (number), status (BalanceStatus imported from src/shared/types/index.ts), createdAt (Date), updatedAt (Date).

ILeaveBalanceRepository interface is defined with method signatures: findById(id: string): Promise<LeaveBalance | null>, findByEmployeeId(employeeId: string): Promise<LeaveBalance[]>, findByEmployeeAndPolicy(employeeId: string, policyId: string): Promise<LeaveBalance | null>, create(balance: Omit<LeaveBalance, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt'>): Promise<LeaveBalance>, update(id: string, balance: Partial<Omit<LeaveBalance, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt'>>): Promise<LeaveBalance | null>, upsert(balance: Omit<LeaveBalance, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt'>): Promise<LeaveBalance>.

LeaveBalanceRepository class extends BaseRepository<LeaveBalance> and implements ILeaveBalanceRepository. Constructor accepts optional Pool override (matching the pattern from LeavePolicyRepository). All six methods execute correct SQL against the leave_balance table using snake_case column mapping.
upsert method uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year) DO UPDATE to atomically create-or-update a balance row, returning the resulting row.

Jest unit tests at tests/unit/modules/leave/leave-balance.repository.test.ts cover all six repository methods with mocked pool.query, verifying correct SQL text, parameter binding, and return-value handling (including null cases for findById and findByEmployeeAndPolicy).

constraints: GP-001: All database access must go through the repository pattern — LeaveBalanceRepository extends BaseRepository and uses the protected query() method for all SQL.

Follow the established pattern from LeavePolicyRepository: snake_case SQL column mapping, dynamic field building in update(), optional Pool override in constructor, soft-delete not applicable (leave_balance has no deleted_at — use the status field for lifecycle).
TypeScript strict mode — no `any` type; use `unknown` for query parameters where needed.
The upsert method must use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year) DO UPDATE, matching the unique constraint declared in ARCHITECTURE.md.
outOfScope: Business logic (balance sufficiency checks, pendingDays arithmetic, policy validation) — deferred to Phase 6 (Leave service).
Audit logging (GP-002) — the repository layer does not write audit records; that responsibility belongs to the service layer in Phase 6.
RBAC enforcement (GP-005) — enforced at the route/middleware layer, not in the repository.
Database migration for the leave_balance table — schema is assumed to exist per ARCHITECTURE.md.

ambiguities.description: The findByEmployeeAndPolicy(employeeId, policyId) method signature does not include fiscalYear, but the unique constraint on leave_balance is (employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year). Without fiscalYear, multiple rows could match. Should the method return the balance for the current fiscal year (derived server-side), accept an optional fiscalYear parameter, or return all matching rows as an array?
options: Return the balance for the current fiscal year (derived from current date server-side in the SQL)
Accept an optional fiscalYear parameter; if omitted, return all matching rows
Accept a required fiscalYear parameter to match the unique constraint exactly
Return Promise<LeaveBalance[]> for all fiscal years
